subject: Three Questions Re Detector Covariates, Trap Availability, and Unmarked Files

messages.author: 1243949a1f9dd1a7
messages.subject: Three Questions Re Detector Covariates, Trap Availability, and Unmarked Files
parts:
This is a three-parter as I'm currently trying to run two separate analyses and having problems with both of them.

First question: I'm trying to do a basic openCR multisession SECR analysis. I've got six years, with the number of detectors varying from 20 to 25 for each year. The detectors are in the same location, but the detector covariate (distance to forest edge) changes with every session. Attached example trap file (ajbtrap1.csv). I make sure to read in the trap files with the covariate name (see attached firstquestioncode). I get this error message: 

Error in openCR.design(capthist, model, type, timecov = timecov, sessioncov = sessioncov,  : 
  covariate(s) DistEd not found
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In reduce.traps(trps, newtraps = newtraps, newoccasions = newoccasions,  :
  covariates vary within groups; using only first

I'm not sure what is happening, but looking at the help file, am I supposed to create a separate data frame with the distance to forest edge covariate values for each year and then include it in the model fitting code?

[attached relevant files: firstquestioncode, ajbtrap1.csv, ajbfana1.csv]

Second question: For the other analysis I'm trying to run a spatial capture mark-resight model including the marking and sighting occasions. I didn't see anything about whether this allows for a multisession analysis, so I was doing a test run on two sessions. Although the marking detectors are all open for the same amount of occasions, the sighting detectors (cameras) aren't. When I tried to include trap availability in the files (see attached testrp1avail.csv and secondquestioncode), I came up with this error message:

Error in read.traps file, differing number in detector and usage

I figured that this might be because this is relatively new in the package, and maybe trap availability isn't ready to be used yet, so I continued on with just a basic trap file that ignores availability. 

 [attached relevant files: secondquestioncode, testdet1.csv, testrp1avail.csv]

Which leads to question three: the creation of the capture history is fine with the basic trap file, but when I try to use addSightings to include the unmarked and marked but unknown individuals, I end up with this error message:

Error in `[.data.frame`(read.table(unmarked, ...), 1:K, 2:(S + 1)) : 
undefined columns selected

I'm sure this is something basic, and might have to do with how I've laid out the file (columns are occasions, rows are detectors), but it looks like the manual, so I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong here either.

[attached relevant files: thirdquestioncode, testdet1.csv, testrp1.csv, TM1.csv, TU1.csv]

Sorry for the long post, I just figured it would be better to have it all in one rather than clutter the group. Thanks for any help!

messages.subject: Re: Three Questions Re Detector Covariates, Trap Availability, and Unmarked Files
parts:
Asia
I think you're expecting too much, both of your data and of the group. From memory, 'usage' in a csv should be in one column per occasion. Check the usage attribute of the traps object you create. I don't think time-varying detector covariates are ever going to work, but there is a workaround where you treat each detector x time as a different detector, and switch them on and off via usage. Maybe start with 'secr' rather than 'openCR' - fewer things to get your head around.
Murray
